blocked_sentences: Station (Tap another creature you control: Put charge counters equal to its power on this Planet. Station only as a sorcery.)
12+ | {U}, {T}: Add {U} for each artifact you control.

needs.what: an activation cost that taps another creature you control and BINDS the creature it tapped, so the ability's own effects can read a characteristic of it. Station's payload is `add_counters` with `counter: "charge"`, `objects: {"self_only": true}` and an amount equal to the tapped creature's power, so the number exists only on the permanent that paid the cost. Concretely: an `as` (binding name) accepted on `cost.tap_permanents`, written into `EffectContext.bindings` by `costs.pay` at the moment each creature is tapped, so the effect can say `amount: {"power_of": {"binding": "stationed"}}`. The creature is chosen at activation (601.2h), so the binding must hold the value as it was then and survive the creature leaving the battlefield or shrinking before the ability resolves -- `snapshot`'s treatment, applied to a cost instead of a target.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `cost.tap_permanents` is the closest existing cost and its pool is already exactly "another creature you control" (`controller`/`types`/`exclude_self` from the selector language, plus crew's `count`/`total_power`), but it is write-only. `costs.pay` (src/automtg/engine/costs.py:1205-1212) resolves the pool, asks for the oids, calls `tap_permanent` on each and drops the list -- nothing is recorded on the ability, on the state or in `ctx.bindings`, so no entry in `value_keys` can name the creature afterwards. `power_of` resolves through `_characteristic` (src/automtg/engine/effects/values.py:340) and accepts only a declared `target`, a `snapshot`, `self`, or a binding some op wrote with `as`; a cost is none of those, and a cost cannot be spelled as a target, because crew and convoke are costs precisely because they are untargeted -- a targeted Station would make the creature protectable and the ability fizzle-able, which it is not. `total_power` does read the pool's summed power but only inside `_tap_cost_pool` (src/automtg/engine/costs.py:1011-1024) to decide payability; the number never reaches the effects. `paid_by` is unrelated: it is a trigger-filter key matched against a spell's mana sources (src/automtg/engine/triggers.py:1253) and is unreachable from an ability's effects. The only spelling that dodges all of this -- `choose_permanents` with `as`, then the `tap` op, then `add_counters` reading `power_of` the binding -- is the approximation the brief forbids: paying with an op moves the payment to resolution, so the ability could be activated with no untapped creature available, could be responded to before anything tapped, and would read the power after the window in which opponents could change it. `sorcery_speed_only` already covers "Station only as a sorcery"; the cost is the whole gap.

needs.what: the printed "N+ |" threshold line: an ability a Planet HAS only while it has N or more charge counters on it (12+ here; the layout also prints 4+ and 8+ tiers). The gate must control the ability's existence, not merely its legality -- below the threshold the ability is not on the permanent at all, so it cannot be activated, copied, granted away, or offered by the UI as an option. It also needs a card-level spelling for the `12+ |` prefix so the residual gate can see one ability claiming that whole printed line. On this card the gated ability is a mana ability whose effect is already sayable (`add_mana_per` with `mana: "{U}"` and `per: {"count": {"controller": "you", "types": ["Artifact"]}}` under a `{U}`+`tap` cost); only the threshold is missing.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: The closest existing thing is `condition` on an activated ability -- `activation_condition` (src/automtg/cards/loader/__init__.py:1596), checked by `_activation_allowed` (src/automtg/engine/legality.py:751) -- which can ask `counters_on` >= 12 through a `cmp`. It refuses the activation but leaves the ability printed on the permanent at every counter count, which is exactly the level-up/Class distinction the mechanic turns on. Nothing in `static_effects` can conditionally add or remove an ability of the SOURCE itself: `grant_ability` points at other objects and `lose_all_abilities` is all-or-nothing, so there is no way to say "this permanent has this ability only while ...". Shipping the `activation_condition` near-miss on each Planet is worse than building the real shape once, because every Planet printed repeats this line.
